title: The animal that survived open space
summary: Tardigrades can dry out into a dormant 'tun' state. In 2007, a Swedish-led experiment showed some survived ten days exposed to the vacuum of space.

scenes.text: Meet the animal that survived open space.
Tardigrades, or 'water bears', are eight-legged animals usually under a millimetre long. They live in moss, soil and oceans.
When their home dries out, they enter a state called a 'tun'.
In 2007, dried tardigrades were sent into orbit on the FOTON-M3 mission.
scenes.reveal: Some survived ten days exposed to space vacuum — a few even survived the Sun's harsh UV too.

scenes.text: The experiment was led by researchers at Kristianstad University in Sweden.
Life can be tougher than we imagine — one reason astrobiologists study it.

sources.title: Tardigrades survive exposure to space in low Earth orbit
